lineage: Linked to the RomCom RAT ecosystem; possible overlap with Industrial Spy
summary: Cuba (Tropical Scorpius / UNC2596) was a double-extortion operation that hit more than 100 organisations, including US critical infrastructure. Its last leak-site post was in February 2024, and Sophos now classes it as inactive. Access came through Hancitor-delivered loaders, ProxyShell/ProxyLogon Exchange exploitation with web shells, and compromised RDP admin credentials. The crew escalated with CVE-2022-24521 (CLFS) and Zerologon, harvested credentials from Veeam via CVE-2023-27532, and blinded EDR with the ApcHelper.sys driver (signed with a leaked NVIDIA certificate) and the BURNTCIGAR process killer before deploying the COLDDRAW/Cuba locker.
uniqueTraits: Kernel driver ApcHelper.sys signed with a certificate from the LAPSUS NVIDIA leak, plus BURNTCIGAR, to terminate security products
Exploited the Veeam Backup & Replication credential-exposure flaw CVE-2023-27532 (2023), CLFS CVE-2022-24521 and Zerologon CVE-2020-1472
Custom tooling: TERMITE in-memory dropper, BUGHATCH downloader, ROMCOM RAT (ICMP-based C2), KerberCache
Spoofed download sites serving trojanised SolarWinds NPM, KeePass, PDF Reader Pro and Advanced IP Scanner (RomCom link)

chain.procedure: Exploits ProxyShell and ProxyLogon on Microsoft Exchange (from about August 2021) and other known flaws in commercial software.
chain.noAtomicReason: No local atomic exploits Exchange ProxyShell or ProxyLogon. Validate with Exchange/IIS log analytics and with the follow-on web-shell step.

chain.procedure: Plants web shells on compromised Exchange servers and uses them to load the TERMITE in-memory dropper and backdoors.

atomics.note: Writes a web shell into a web-server directory.

chain.procedure: 2023 campaign: signs in over RDP with compromised admin credentials, with no brute forcing involved.

atomics.note: An RDP logon with valid credentials generates the logon telemetry. The credential theft that comes before it is not reproduced.

chain.procedure: Brings in payloads with the Hancitor loader (earlier campaigns) and the custom BUGHATCH downloader (2022–2023), which fetch RATs, Cobalt Strike and the ransomware.

atomics.note: Downloads a file with PowerShell, standing in for the BUGHATCH fetch.

chain.procedure: The ROMCOM RAT backdoor talks to its C2 over ICMP requests and offers reverse shell and file deletion.
Exploits the Windows CLFS driver flaw CVE-2022-24521 to steal SYSTEM tokens, and Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) to get Domain Admin.
chain.noAtomicReason: The local catalogue has no CLFS or Zerologon exploit test, and exploit code is out of scope. Use Netlogon event 5829 analytics, SYSTEM-token theft telemetry and patch validation instead.

chain.procedure: 2023: exploits the Veeam Backup & Replication flaw CVE-2023-27532 to pull credentials stored in the Veeam configuration database.
chain.noAtomicReason: No local atomic targets Veeam's credential store or CVE-2023-27532. Cover it with Veeam service and SQL access monitoring.

chain.techniqueName: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
chain.procedure: Kerberoasts with a PowerShell script and cracks the tickets offline.

atomics.note: Requests all SPN tickets from PowerShell.

chain.procedure: Uses KerberCache to pull cached Kerberos tickets out of LSASS memory.

atomics.testName: Dump Kerberos Tickets from LSA using dumper.ps1
atomics.note: Dumps Kerberos tickets from LSA with dumper.ps1. The ticket-extraction goal is the same; KerberCache itself is not used.

chain.procedure: After running the CLFS exploit, uses ADFind and NetScan to discover AD objects and hosts for lateral movement.

atomics.testName: Adfind - Enumerate Active Directory User Objects

chain.procedure: A dropper writes the kernel driver ApcHelper.sys (signed with a leaked NVIDIA certificate) to find and terminate security products. BURNTCIGAR kills security processes, and aswArPot.sys also appears in the IOCs.

atomics.testName: Kill antimalware protected processes using Backstab
atomics.note: Kills protected security processes through a signed kernel driver (Backstab), the same driver-assisted kill pattern.

atomics.testName: Scattered Spider BYOVD (CVE-2015-2291 for Intel Ethernet Diagnostics Driver)
atomics.note: Loads a known-vulnerable signed driver as a kernel service, BYOVD-style.

chain.procedure: Moves laterally with RDP sessions and Impacket.

atomics.note: Opens an RDP session to a remote host.

chain.procedure: Uses Cobalt Strike and Metasploit/Meterpreter, with HTTP/HTTPS proxying through the C2 server.

atomics.testName: Cobalt Strike post-exploitation pipe (4.2 and later)
atomics.note: Creates Cobalt Strike post-exploitation named pipes.
HTTP C2 with suspicious user agents.

chain.procedure: Steals data before encryption and leaks it on the group's shaming site (double extortion). No specific exfiltration tool is named.

atomics.note: Exfiltrates data over a C2-style HTTP channel.

chain.procedure: Deploys the Cuba/COLDDRAW encryptor (.cuba extension) for double extortion. The last victim post was in February 2024.

atomics.note: Drops a ransom note artifact. The encryptor itself is not reproduced.
